version.changelog: A failed call is never audited ok: interrupted status, typer>=0.26 exits, result credential scrubbing, lost audit rows visible and self-healing, runaway guard on real arguments.

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed VMware audit and policy helper, but users should treat its external package install and local audit database as sensitive operational trust points.

dimensions.detail: Local Bash/CLI use, ~/.vmware state, and reading only the presence of selected agent environment variables are coherent with audit and policy infrastructure, but the audit database can contain sensitive operational data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The main install is pinned to vmware-policy==1.16.0 via uv, with source linked, but the reviewed artifact does not include implementation code or require hash/signature verification; related package examples are less tightly pinned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to installing vmware-policy, querying/exporting audit logs, configuring local rules, and integrating decorators; the documentation overstates sanitize() as prompt-injection prevention, but does not hide unrelated behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent files under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME, hot-reloaded rules, audit rotation, and undo descriptors are disclosed and purpose-aligned; no cron, service, backdoor, or hidden startup persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, metadata, and references consistently describe audit logging, optional policy checks, CLI audit queries, and sanitization for the VMware skill family; the artifact says it exposes no MCP tools itself.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you trust the vmware-policy package source and the VMware skill family. Protect ~/.vmware because audit rows may contain infrastructure details, configure VMware RBAC and explicit deny rules for production, do not rely on default policy or sanitize() alone as a safety boundary, and avoid leaving VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 set.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The kubeconfig/token/password references are credential-redaction examples and sensitive-result handling for audit rows, not instructions to read credential stores.
[PE2] expected: The chmod commands set restrictive permissions on the local audit directory/database and do not request sudo or root execution.
[RA2] expected: The ~/.vmware audit.db, rules.yaml, and undo.db files are disclosed local state for audit and policy operation, not unauthorized cross-session control.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited text discusses policy rules and optional vmware-pilot approval routing; this artifact does not itself automate high-impact VMware actions.
[E3] expected: The ls command is a narrow troubleshooting check of ~/.vmware/rules.yaml mtime, not broad filesystem enumeration.
[T08] expected: External uv/GitHub installation is the documented install path and is purpose-aligned, though it leaves a supply-chain trust boundary because hashes or signatures are not required.
[T09] expected: The sanitizer is a disclosed feature, but character stripping and truncation should be treated as partial hardening rather than complete semantic prompt-injection prevention.
